Once I had my commercial license, I continued to compete, only now it was against other commercial mead producers. Sometimes that can be exhilarating, and sometimes it can be humbUng -- but it aU adds up to educating the mead maker and that makes for better product for the consumer.

I reached out to facilities that could help manage the receiving and storage of competition entries and host the judging sessions. The first obstacle I encountered was that the locations I spoke with already held a liquor license, and that license would prevent them from hosting a competition in their venue.
I reached out to the organizers of competitions. When I asked Kevin IVteintsma, the organizer of Minnesota's Valkyries' Horn competition how they did it, he said they wrote competitions into Minnesota State law. That sounded daunting, but it made sense to
me.

I reached out to BABLO for suggestions and for the details about current law, and what would need to be addressed to make hosting a compeddon compliant with BABLO. Then I reached out to Representative Shagoury about sponsoring this biU, and he was interested in helping bring this idea to life. So to sum up - with this biU we hope to create a simple "permitted competition" where a competition - being a standardized evaluation of alcoholic beverages, can be organized and held here in Maine, and the related logistics (receiving and storing of entries, and the opening, tasdng and judging of entries both commercial and homebrew) can be done in compliance with BABLO law.

have.

Testimony of Representative Dan Shagoury introducing
LD 1033, An Act to Regulate Alcoholic Beverage Competitions Before the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs

Good morning, Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. I am Representative Dan Shagoury, and I represent House District 55 - the communities ofHallowell, Manchester and West Gardiner. I come before you today to introduce LD 1033, An Act to Regulate Alcoholic Beverage Competitions.

The background for this bill is very straightforward. One of my constituents, Christy Hemenway, runs a meadery in West Gardiner. About a year ago, she approached me with the idea for this bill. She explained to me that she was looking into holding a judged competition for mead and found that the laws in Maine do not allow for the type of event she had in mind. She then asked me if I would be willing to submit a bill to make the necessary adjustment to the law to allow for competitions, and I agreed.

She explained that the kind of judged competition they have in other states doesn't only provide a fun opportunity to try a variety of different meads, but also allows for them to be rated against each other. The judges would not only taste the mead and rank them, but also state what each mead's strengths and weaknesses are. This helps the makers improve their product.

My constituent will be speaking after me, and I think any questions about these types of competitions would be best saved for her. Even though I have learned a lot about mead, tasting competitions and Maine's alcoholic beverage laws over the last year, I am still far from an
expert.

Briefly, what this bill will do is define the parameters of these events and make the necessary exceptions to the law to allow for a small number of authorized Judged competitions to be permitted each year.

We have been working with BABLO through the development of this bill, and they have some suggested amendments I would like made to the bill. They will provide testimony in more detail concerning these changes, but on their recommendation, I would like to amend the bill in the following ways:

Testimony of the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs
Neither For Nor Against LD 1033 An Act to Regulate Alcoholic Beverage Competitions
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs: I am Louis Luchini and I'm the Director of the Bureau of Alcoholic Beverages and Lottery Operations. We are submitting testimony neither for nor against LD 1033, An Act to Regulate Alcoholic Beverage Competitions.
The Bureau appreciates the collaboration with Rep. Shagoury and his constituent, Christy Hemenway, in developing the bill. We believe alcohol competitions must be well regulated to ensure public safety. Based on our discussions, we are recommending a few changes for the committee's consideration.
First, we are opposed to the provision allowing homemade spirits to be included in competitions. You may recall that BABLO opposed LD 631, An Act to Allow a Home Distiller to Distill and Share Homemade Spirituous Liquor. This bill takes home distilling further by allowing home distillers to provide samples to the public. We recommend either striking spirits from the bill or limiting participation to licensed spirits manufacturers.
Second, we recommend that the eligibility for a competition permit be limited to licensees or certificate of approval holders - not individual home producers. Licensees are well versed in Maine's alcohol laws and are experienced in serving alcohol to members of the public. That experience is important in ensuring events are conducted safely. We'd further recommend clarifying who may participate in these competitions, whether it's licensed entities or home producers.
Some other states that allow competitions establish parameters through rulemaking. We think it makes sense for BABLO to promulgate rules for these events.
Lastly, in conversations with the bill's sponsor, we have discussed the possibility of hosting competitions in conjunction with national organizations who run these types of events across the country. We are still considering this possibility, and wanted to mention it for the committee's consideration.
Thanks for your time. BABLO is happy to work with the sponsor and legislators to develop this proposal and will be available for the work session at the committee's request.
